target: plant organ margin (PO_0025005) part_of perianth tube (FLOPO_0986010)
reason: A perianth cup is the cup-shaped fused part of the perianth (Lauraceae, Proteaceae, Thymelaeaceae), which here is the perianth tube. Its margin is the margin region of that whole, which the part-of-a-qualified-whole pattern can express. If a flora uses 'perianth cup' for a receptacular cup, the whole is instead hypanthium (PO_0009065; 'floral cup' is a PO synonym).

target: pinnate (PATO_0000410) on the leaf; the number is the order of division
reason: This is a quality, not a part. '3-5-pinnately compound' gives the number of times the leaf is pinnately divided. The previous review treated 'palmately compound' the same way (rule:pato digitate).

The axis of a fern pinnule is its costule, the midrib of the pinnule. It is expressed as the midvein region of the pinnule class, in the same way as pinna rachis (FLOPO_0986065) one order up. This is narrower than leaf midvein.

label: pollen pore
parent: is_a plant anatomical space (PO_0025117); part_of pollen (PO_0025281)
definition: A more or less circular aperture in the wall of a pollen grain, with a length:width ratio of less than 2, through which the pollen tube may emerge.
reason: Pollen pores are a standard palynological character in Flora Malesiana, Flora Neotropica and others, and PO has no pollen wall or aperture class. PO's 'canal' (PO_0025132) lists colpus as a synonym, but its definition (a groove or tube) does not fit a pore. Count statements ('3-4-porate') should also get a counted-parts rule (porate → pollen pore on pollen). This should be proposed upstream to PO together with a pollen aperture parent.

These are the calli on an orchid labellum disc. 'Rows of' is a count of rows, not a part. Callus has no fitting class: PO_0005052 is tissue-culture callus, and FLOPO_0986120 is the grass floret callus. The previous review rejected bare 'callus' as a generic part.

Without context this is ambiguous: it could be vein-bounded leaf lamina areoles in ferns (PO_0025392) or cactus areoles (PO_0025353 areole bud). 'Rows of' is a count of rows. The previous review rejected bare 'areole'.

'Rows of' is a count of rows. PO has no generic spine class, only spine leaf (PO_0025173), spine stipule (PO_0025174), thorn (PO_0025172) and prickle (PO_0025169), and these cannot be told apart from 'bearing 8 rows'.
This is the lobe of a pinnule. 'Secondary' gives the order of division and is not a separate structure. It is narrower than phyllome lamina lobe.
This joins two generic parts without the organ they belong to. The previous review rejected bare 'segment'.
'Short' is a quality. Without context the spur could be a floral spur (FLOPO_0986133) or a spur shoot (short shoot, PO_0004701).

This is narrower than leaf lamina vein. PO gives veinlet as a synonym of the secondary, tertiary, quaternary and higher-order leaf vein classes, so the shared parent is the safe target. 'Simple' is the quality unbranched (PATO_0000414).

This is the plural of spine, which should be lemmatized. PO has no generic spine class (spine leaf, spine stipule, thorn, prickle, or the emergence FLOPO_0986107), and these examples ('2 erect spines', 'a row of spines on the...') do not say which.
This is a fragment: two alternative parts joined by 'or'. It should be split, and tubercle (PO_0025352) already exists. The pair is not a structure.
This is a quality word left over from '3-10 pairs of spinose teeth'. The bearer is leaf lamina tooth (PO_0025518).
'Spinulose' is a quality, and a 'projection' can be any outgrowth. The example does not say which organ it belongs to.
Spots are a colour pattern, which is a quality of the organ that bears them, not a plant structure. The previous review rejected 'spot'.

This is narrower than flower. These are the enlarged sterile marginal flowers of Hydrangea and Viburnum cymes. Sterile, radiant (enlarged, showy) and marginal are qualities or positions. Ray flower (PO_0025331) does not fit, because it is a floret of a capitulum.

This is narrower than portion of secretory tissue; gland is a PO synonym of that class, and the previous review grounded 'gland' the same way. 'Stipitate' is a quality, and 'basal' is a position on the described organ (plant organ base, FLOPO_0985024).
This is a fragment: two alternative parts joined by 'or'. They should be split into tooth and lobe, which are already counted parts.
This is a fragment: two alternative parts joined by 'or'. 'Segment' is generic.
This is narrower than bract. 'Terminal' is a position in the series, which the patterns can express.

This is an exact match, with 'axi' a lemmatizer error for axes. In 'tertiary axes 5-15 per secondary', the axes are counted in panicle order: main axis, then secondary axes (second order, PO_0006321), then tertiary axes (third order). PO's 'tertiary inflorescence branch' is the fourth-order axis, so map by axis order, not by the branch synonym. If these come from fern fronds, they need a different target.

reason: This is a quality: '3 or 4 times pinnately branched' gives the order of division.
This is narrower than portion of secretory tissue (PO synonym: gland). 'Tuberculate' is a shape quality.

This is narrower than leaf sheath. It means bladeless basal leaves reduced to sheaths (Eleocharis, Juncus, the sheath at the base of an Eriocaulon scape). 'Tubular' is a quality and 'at base' is a position. Scale leaf (PO_0006003) is the alternative if a flora means cataphylls.
This is an orientation word left over from '3 vertical furrows/grooves'. The part is furrow or groove, both PO synonyms of canal (PO_0025132).
This is an arrangement quality, not a part.
'With 2 winged flanges' does not say which organ the flanges belong to: fruit, seed or stem. 'Winged' is a quality.
